messages:
maya: Heads up, the infra repo CI is spamming retries on the gpu-provision matrix jobs after the cache eviction at ~23:10. Lots of concurrent terraform applies.

sam: Seeing it too, lots of `apply` attempts stacking up. failed during `google_container_node_pool` create with 504 timeouts.

ci-bot: [gha] job gpu-provision/matrix(6/12) failed — Retrying (attempt 3/3) — response: timeout after 300s. logs: ```Error: RPC failed: deadline exceeded
2024-04-12T23:10:05Z provisioning: create nodepool: http 504```

lee: Looks like runner cache eviction triggered a bunch of matrix jobs to rehydrate layers at the same time, blowing out egress and hitting provider rate limits.

alex: @maya do we know which cache key got evicted? my guess is the docker-layer cache for the gpu image. If re-pulls are simultaneous they hammer the registry and our NAT egress.

maya: infra-bot posted eviction event to #eng-infra earlier: `eviction: runner-cache-s3/object gc triggered, removed keys: runners/docker-layer-*` — that matches the timeline.

sam: Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) cancel duplicate in-flight runs for the same PR, 2) disable matrix retries temporarily, 3) add randomized backoff on job start. Thoughts?

lee: Cancelling duplicates would help. We can wire `concurrency: group: repo-${{ github.ref }}-terraform` in workflows so new runs cancel old ones. Also add `max-parallel: 1` for the terraform apply job.

alex: For the cache problem longer-term: pin docker layers to a shared ECR cache, and make the cache key include commit hash so we don't force full rehydrate on unrelated changes. Also consider `actions/cache` fallback warming job to stagger pulls.

maya: Quick patch: I've disabled the workflow-level `retry` util in .github/workflows/infra.yml and triggered a manual cancel for the oldest runs. Cancelling now saved another 6 concurrent applies.

ci-bot: [gha] run canceled — 1755554302 (by maya) :white_check_mark:

lee: Another practical tweak: add `conditional-sleep` step before terraform init for matrix jobs: `sleep $((RANDOM % 30))` to scatter starts. Ugly but effective until we fix underlying eviction pattern.

alex: Agree. Also add S3 lifecycle guard so runner-cache eviction doesn't prune within 6 hours for active runner pools. Ops should review TTL.

sam: I'll open a tiny PR with `concurrency` + `sleep` + disable retries. Also a follow-up issue for scheduler to avoid stampedes when caches are cold.

maya: Thanks — FYI logs snippet for the terraform collision: ```apply: starting apply (run id=1755554310)
lock: acquired by run 1755554310
apply: provider error, retrying...
apply: starting apply (run id=1755554312)
lock: cannot acquire lock, retrying...
apply: run 1755554310 timed out, lock released unexpectedly -> both runs tried to finish same resources -> partial state corruption risk```

lee: That partial state risk is why we need to ensure only one apply per infra branch. BTW checkstate & remote state locking are fine, but GHA retries bypassed lock delays which caused the stampede.

alex: I'll take the follow-up to add the S3 lock TTL tweak and safe cache eviction policy. Sam, ping me on the PR.

sam: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/788 — includes `concurrency` group and 0-30s randomized `sleep` step.

maya: Merged and rolled out. Waiting for queue to drain. Keeping retries off for the next 24h.

infra-bot: maintenance-notice: runner-cache retention increased to 6h for pool `gha-ubuntu-gpu`, scheduled GC window moved to 03:00 UTC.

sam: Queue stabilized, subsequent matrix jobs started staggered and no new provider 504s. Re-enabling controlled retries after monitoring window.

maya: Follow-ups: 1) infra task to move docker-layer cache to ECR + warming job, 2) add per-PR concurrency group to all infra workflows, 3) monitoring alert for sudden cache eviction spikes. I'll file tickets.

lee: Thanks everyone — good catch. We'll also document the `do-not-retry-on-provider-504` rule in runbooks. :thumbsup:

alex: Closing thread when follow-ups are in issues. Great work mitigating quickly.
